steps.text: Cook and stir sausage in a large skillet over medium heat until browned. Drain.

Add tomato sauce, diced tomatoes, bay leaves, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, basil, oregano, salt, and pepper to Italian sausage in the skillet. Simmer sauce over medium-low heat for at least 1 hour, or longer for deeper flavor.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook spaghetti in boiling water until tender yet firm to the bite, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain and transfer to a large serving bowl.
Add pasta to simmering sauce; toss until evenly coated. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Hearty Italian Sausage Spaghetti
raw_recipe.description: The Italian spaghetti is easy to make with sausage, canned tomato sauce, diced tomatoes, and herbs for a hearty, no-fuss dinner the whole family will love.

review.reviewBody: This sauce was amazing! My friend raved over the smell when she came in my front door. She said it smelled like "real sauce". When she tasted it her exact words "It's just right. Not to sweet and not to spicy". I will definitely make this again. My one suggestion would be to make sure you use the Italian Sausage, I don't think it would be as good with out the extra kick from the seasonings of the sausage.

This recipe is THE best! I had a similar experience as the last person who commented...my boyfriend walked in the door and said he could smell the sauce from outside our home and that it smelled fanstastic. I stayed completely true to the recipe except for a couple of things-which were only due to personal preference. I used 1 lb of ground beef instead of sausage and added half of a chopped white onion while seasoning beef. Also added 1/2 teaspoon of red pepper flakes that gave the sauce a small zing. We LOVED it and both agreed this recipe will be a staple in our home. Thank you so much for submitting this :-)

This was a very good sauce. I used a whole pound of sausage, because I had a pound in the freezer that I wanted to use. Great flavor. I used fresh basil and oregano, but added those at the end. I did add some dried in the beginning. Also used 3 cloves fresh garlic, and some dried onion. I used two larger cans of tomato sauce (14 oz?) instead of the smaller ones and one can was no-salt-added. This sauce was still a little too salty for me, probably because of the evaporated liquid during the long simmer. The long simmer is essential though (I did a little over an hour) to develop that great thick texture and great flavor. Mine got a little too thick, so I added a splash of water at the end. Served over whole-wheat spaghetti.
Everyone loves this recipe. I use it exactly as shown, but use the italian diced tomatoes with spices. I also use a crock pot and cook for 4 - 6 hours and it turns out absolutely fabulous!

I made this recipe and it was very tasty. The second time, I switched a few things. I used 3 cloves of minced fresh garlic, a finely chopped onion, and I squeezed the sausage from its casing for a more crumbly texture. I also used one one bay leaf but added about 15 fresh basil leaves (sliced thinly). I also splashed about a teaspoon of balsamic vinegar and a teaspoon of salt—I don’t know what it necessarily did but it felt chef-like and as though I knew what I was doing. It was a really tasty version and my family said they liked it better (they were not aware I had played with the recipe). Highly recommend either! The sauce freezes really well for future meals, too! :)

Very good restaurant quality spaghetti sauce! I used no salt added tomatoes and 32 oz of tomato sauce (4 8 oz cans) and did not add additional salt. Served over spaghetti instead of mixing it in. I simmered the sauce for a couple of hours and the recipe made 5 cups of sauce. This is now my go to spaghetti sauce recipe! I think next time I'll add in some mushrooms (just because we love them, it is perfect as is).

We didn't have enough cans of the tomato sauce however we had tons of fresh tomatoes and tomato paste so we made it work. Also added sauteed onion and garlic, as well as fennel seed and rosemary. Tasty.

Delicious as is but for my family we use a full # of meat and generally I double the recipe and use 1# lean gr beef and 1# turkey Italian saus. Also, browned 1 med onion and fresh garlic with meat for dbld recipe. I also use 1-26.5 oz box POMI finely chopped tomatoes and 2-26oz boxes POMI strained tomatoes for dbld recipe. May need additional seasonings to taste as POMI a is all natural. (Salt/more Italian seasoning and I add rd pepper flakes)

Made it just using the ingredients listed on the recipe. Did however use 1 24oz can of tomato sauce. Other than that, the recipe makes a good spaghetti sauce meal We are a family of cheese lovers, so at the end I added some parmesan cheese as a topping and as a side had garlic bread with olive oil and balsamic vinegar dipping sauce. Turned out to be a good meal and the wife wants me to make it again. If she likes it, then it’s got to be good.
Delicious! This was a huge hit with my family. I followed the recipe exactly except I used a whole pound of sausage since that was what the package was.

My family and I love this recipe! I used a pound of mild italian sausage and to cut down on the sodium I used 3 of the 6.5 cans of the no salt tomato sauce and 1 regular one, then continued with the rest of the ingredients. Simmer it up to 6-7 hrs. It turned out perfect. My 10yr old eats it all up every time. Thanks for the recipe!
Tried this recipe last night. My son and daughter-in-law were over and everyone loved it. Easy to follow and will definitely make again.

Excellent sauce recipe, I just added a bit of burrito seasoning (my personal mix) to add a little heat. I have been a fan of “fried spaghetti”, and this is great! I live alone and cook only for myself, so 1 to 1.5 cups is a meal. I heat a couple Tbls of avocado oil and fry it (about pancake size) until it’s just becoming lightly crisp on each side. The frying gives this a touch of extra flavor that you don’t want to miss. The cooked pasta and sauce freeze well also!

This is how my spaghetti sauce always starts out but I also add diced onions, green bell pepper, sliced mushrooms and once in a while throw in sliced black olives. Then let it simmer for at least an hour, refrigerate and serve it the next day, cuz it's even better then!

This was 5 stars as is and I am true to try new recipes as author intended. I will make again for sure. I will incorporate some fresh diced onion and garlic next time as I prefer the added flavor and textures. I simmered for 1 hour and next time will simmer for 2+ so the ingredients break down a little more for a smooth sauce. This is a keeper!
Very strong tomato taste, I added sugar and broth to adjust the acidity
I used a can of crushed tomatoes, instead of tomato sauce (poor planning on my part) last time I made this - we liked it just as well.
I used 1 lb of hot Italian sausage and sautéed onions and bell peppers with the sausage. Used fresh garlic instead of garlic powder. It was good but I will stick to my regular recipe.
Made this as written although I didn’t add the sausage. It is perfect

I only made a few changes after I fried the sausage up completely as I had it draining and set to the side I put 2 tablespoons of butter in my skillet after the butter melted I added all the seasonings that are in the original recipe but I also added one pack of mushroom and onion dry soup mix then I added my sausage back to the skillet and added the spaghetti sauce after the noodles were done cooking I mixed everything together I put cheese on top of it and I baked it in the oven at 350 for about 15 minutes covered with aluminum foil
